pick.title: Choose a computer in Browse
pick.body: The commands here are for the computer on the From side of Browse.
need.title: Install the Hoody CLI
need.cli: Once on your PC: install, then sign in.
need.cliLabel: Install the Hoody CLI and sign in
need.rclone: v1.61.0 or newer, from rclone.org (Homebrew's rclone can't mount on a Mac). Packages from Linux distributions may be older.
mount.title: Put {{name}}'s files on your PC
mount.label: Commands that put {{name}}'s files on your PC
mount.unmount: Unmount the whole computer (waits for files still uploading)
mount.force: Unmount the whole computer without waiting
mount.signIn: The CLI signs in on its own, so this Hub session cannot limit what it changes. This session can't change files: use the read-only line if you only need to read.
mount.forceNote: Without waiting, files not yet sent stay in the mount's cache until you run the same mount again (same computer, same folder there, same PC folder).
mount.rules: {{name}} has access rules: add --auth-token-file <file> or --auth-password-file <file> to the mount command.
mount.rulesUnknown: If {{name}} has access rules, add --auth-token-file <file> or --auth-password-file <file> to the mount command.
share.title: Put a PC folder into {{name}}
share.label: Commands that put a PC folder into {{name}}
share.deletes: While it runs, the folder is a place in Browse. Deleting there deletes the files on your PC.
notOffered: SFTP, scp and SSH forwarding aren't offered: the public SSH gateway refuses them.
mount.unmountFolder: Unmount only {{folder}} (waits for files still uploading)
shell.posix: These lines are for a macOS or Linux terminal.
shell.quote: In Windows PowerShell, write each ' inside a quoted path as '' instead of '\''.
share.signIn: This session can't change files, so the read-only line comes first: with it, {{name}} can read the folder but not change or delete files on your PC.
nocli.noAddress: {{name}}'s files program has no address yet, so it can't be opened as a network drive. Use the CLI lines below.
sdk.title: Mount from your code
sdk.body: The Hoody SDK mounts {{name}}'s files on a folder from JavaScript or TypeScript:
sdk.label: Mount with the Hoody SDK
need.rclone.label: rclone
need.mac.label: macOS
need.windows.label: Windows
need.windows: WinFsp. The mount runs in the foreground there.
need.linux.label: Linux
atGlance.title: About this computer
atGlance.rules.open: None: the address is the key
atGlance.rules.set: Set: mount lines need a token or password file
mount.more: More lines: background, list, unmount without waiting
mount.moreLabel: More commands for {{name}}'s files on your PC
address.mount: By the files address, without signing in (the address is the key)
address.unmount: Unmount the folder mounted by the address
way.title: What do you want to do?
way.body: Pick one. The steps below are for that choice only.
way.folder: Work on {{name}}'s files in a folder on your PC
way.folder.what: Open, edit and save them with your own programs, at any size. Needs the Hoody CLI.
way.drive: Open them as a network drive
way.drive.what: Nothing to install: Finder, File Explorer or GNOME Files. Best for a quick look and small files.
way.share: Give {{name}} a folder from your PC
way.share.what: The folder shows up inside {{name}} while a command runs on your PC. Needs the Hoody CLI.
way.code.what: Mount {{name}}'s files from JavaScript or TypeScript with the Hoody SDK.
drive.title: Open {{name}}'s files as a network drive
need.m.npx.note: Needs Node.js. Installs nothing: in later lines, write npx hoody-sdk in place of hoody.
need.moreBody: Install these once. The lines in the next step stop without them.
mount.get: {{name}}'s files show up in {{dir}}, and what you save there goes back.
share.get: A folder such as ~/Projects/site appears in {{name}} at /hoody/mounts/permanent/site for as long as the command runs.
sdk.install: Add the Hoody SDK to your project
sdk.installBody: Run one of these in your project's folder.
sdk.noAddress: {{name}}'s files program has no address yet, so there is nothing to mount from your code.
atGlance.body: The computer these steps are for.
need.m.unix.note: Paste the first line into a terminal, then sign in.
drive.body: Paste this address on your device.
